Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Wednesday printed the follow-through day the group has been waiting for — QQQ +2.31% at 690.38 on 1.14x prior-day volume, back above the 200-day SMA 681.71, with the Day 1 low intact after the Nov 5 undercut — and SPY +1.32% to 759.81, above its 8 and 21 EMAs but still 0.25% under the 50-day EMA. Venu supplies the confirmation and the caution in the same post: the FTD checks all four boxes, but “most semis still below 200-day SMA, lower highs, no reclaim yet — index can bounce while leaders lag.” Sean supplies the intraday frame: Day 4 of the rally attempt, QQQ back over the 200 SMA, SPY right under the 1.25% threshold at midday — at the close both conditions were met. Remz supplies the flow: a 14,000x opener in the SPY 770 calls for Nov 27, $6.57M premium. And then the day's real story broke after the bell. The Jensen Huang story — WSJ, per DiCarlo, with neither Jensen nor NVDA having commented yet — sent NVDA ~8% lower after hours (~$159.60 per Prof's chart, ~$158.76 per iain's, both below the 52-week low 165.17) while AMD added another 4.26% after hours to ~$576.52, on top of its +7.32% session. Prof supplies the scoreboard: AMD has added over $100 billion in market cap since the scandal broke — and “expect more negative news.” iain supplies the warning to the dip-buyers: “Stocks don't go on discount, they trend” — the “on sale” crowd keeps catching a falling knife. Remz supplies the trade: “Watch to see where the money from $NVDA goes. Those names will be your biggest winners now” — and raised his AMD target to $1,000 for 2027. DiCarlo supplies the contrarian read: “I don't think the board removes Jensen.” Enrich supplies the rest of the board: his 11/12 watchlist (AMD, AVGO, UBER, GOOGL, BE, NFLX, DIS), the UBER $100 call with the daily/weekly/monthly setup and EMAs compressing into a three-year consolidation, and the Leadr call contracts for tomorrow (ABBV $300C, COST $1,100C, PG $170C, LLY $1,500C, MO $80C) — all “watching for confirmation before entry” — plus the consumer names holding up overnight (LLY, ABBV, COST, PG, DIS). Your process gives two genuine qualifiers with triggers above the close: COST (0.61% under its high, Enrich's $1,100 strike 1.14% above the close) and PG (0.59% under its high, $170 strike 1.39% above) — plus AMD as a breakout out of the demand zone that is now extended after a two-leg news move, and UBER as a base to watch below a falling 30-week MA. The extended names tell the other half: BE (+12.97% day, still below its 30-week MA), LLY/ABBV/DIS at their 52-week highs with no pullback, MO 0.82% under its high, and NVDA — five traders talking, none calling a buy. The discipline is in the framing: the follow-through day confirms the rally attempt, but the leadership question and the NVDA shock decide whether it holds — and Thursday's open, with NVDA indicated below its 52-week low, is the first test.

  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid).   • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
